title: Human Classifier Simulation
goals: Construct a classifier with a stated input format, selected rule and recorded output
Trace valid, boundary and invalid inputs through different paths
Distinguish an input check from evidence that a prediction is correct
vocabulary: A procedure that assigns a predicted category to an input
The format and conditions an input must satisfy for a procedure to accept it
Checking whether an input satisfies the stated contract
An explicit outcome when the classifier does not assign a category
A name that identifies the particular model used for a prediction

blocks.text: A valid 9 cm input receives a tall prediction, but the input check does not establish that the prediction matches its comparison label. Validation checks the contract. Evaluation checks predictions against appropriate evidence. Keep these questions separate.

Sixty millimetres equals six centimetres, but this version accepts cm records only. It does not contain a conversion step. Ask for a correctly recorded cm measurement or deliberately design and check a conversion step in a new version. Do not silently treat the digits 60 as centimetres. A missing height must not become an invented zero either.

guided_practice.title: Construct both outcome paths
guided_practice.prompt: Write numbered instructions for Tower1, including input checks, the stopping path after a failed check, the threshold rule and the record to keep. Your partner must be able to use them without supplying an unstated rule.
guided_practice.answer: Check present height and cm unit, then whole number in 1 through 10. On failure, record original input, Tower1, no prediction and the reason; stop that record. Otherwise predict tall if height is at least 6, short otherwise. Record original input, Tower1 and prediction. Equivalent clear branches are acceptable.

independent_case.title: Changed independent case
independent_case.task: A written rule selects science books with fewer than 140 pages. Trace science/139, science/140, history/90 and missing-genre/90. Policy: missing required information means request it.
independent_case.answer: Select science/139. Reject science/140 at the strict boundary and history/90 on genre. Request the missing genre rather than inventing it. Both conditions are required.

misconceptions: Any numeric input must receive a category
Check the stated unit, whole-number condition and supported range before comparing the threshold.
An accepted input proves a correct prediction
Ask separately whether the input satisfies the contract and whether the prediction agrees with evaluation evidence.
No prediction means a third category of tower
It is a system outcome indicating that no short or tall category was assigned.
Writing a rejection is enough even if processing continues
Follow the failed path to an explicit stop so the later rule cannot overwrite the outcome.

blocks.title: Three records through the Tower1 classifier
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right. An accepted input reaches the threshold rule. A missing input stops before that rule and receives an explicit no prediction outcome.

blocks.text: For every record, first check that a height is present and its stated unit is cm. Then check that it is a whole number from 1 through 10. If any check fails, record no prediction and the reason, then stop processing that record. Do not continue into the threshold comparison.

If all checks pass, compare the height with 6. At least 6 gives the prediction tall; otherwise give short. Record the original input, model version Tower1 and the prediction. For a rejected record, record the original input, Tower1, no prediction and a reason. Tower1 identifies the intended model even when its threshold was not used.
